data.one_liner: A MySQL and MariaDB database driver for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Allows connecting to MySQL and MariaDB databases to execute SQL queries, inserts, updates, and handle results. Works on both Flutter (non-web) and server-side Dart.
use_when: You need to connect a Dart or Flutter application directly to a MySQL or MariaDB database
You want an API similar to package:postgres for MySQL
avoid_when: You are targeting Flutter Web, as sockets are not supported
You need an ORM or higher-level query builder like drift
strengths: Easy to use interface close to major MySQL drivers and package:postgres
Supports secure connections using SSL and modern authentication methods like caching_sha2_password
weaknesses: Does not work on Flutter Web because it opens raw sockets
Parameters are bound client-side as literals rather than using server-side prepared statements
data.setup_notes: Requires a running MySQL or MariaDB database and proper network/socket access (not supported on Flutter Web).

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose sqflite if you need embedded SQLite storage locally on mobile devices rather than a remote MySQL server.

alternatives.name: sqlite3
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose sqlite3 for raw SQLite database access in Dart and Flutter.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose drift if you want a type-safe reactive ORM layer for SQLite databases.
